lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Why are you strangling Helen, Protesilaus? You came at her like a man repossessing furniture.

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: Because of her, Aeacus, I died with my house half-built and my bride still new enough to be called a bride. I left her a widow before the wedding dust had settled.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Then blame Menelaus. He was the one who dragged you all to Troy over a woman like that.

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: Fair. Yes. He is the one I should be blaming.

lines.speaker: Menelaus
lines.text: Not me, my good man. More properly Paris: my guest, who carried off my wife in open contempt of every law of hospitality. If anyone deserves throttling, not just by you but by every Greek and barbarian alive—well, formerly alive—it is that man. He caused all those deaths.

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: Better. In that case, Paris, you disaster, I am never taking my hands off you.

lines.speaker: Paris
lines.text: You would be doing me an injustice, Protesilaus, especially since I am in the same line of work as you. I too am a man in love. I was seized by the same god. You know how it is: there is nothing voluntary about it. Some power takes us where it likes, and resisting it is impossible.

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: Fair. If only I could get my hands on Eros down here.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: I can give you the legal position on Eros as well. He might say he was responsible for Paris falling in love. Possibly. But for your death, Protesilaus, he will say no one was responsible but you: you forgot that new bride of yours, and when you came up on the Troad you jumped out ahead of the rest—reckless, suicidal, in love with glory. That is why you were the first man killed in the landing.

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: Then let me give you the better legal position on myself, Aeacus. I was not responsible for any of that either. Fate was. The thread had been spun that way from the beginning.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Correct. So why are you blaming them?
